# Hailo Raspberry Pi 5 Examples
[![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/hailo-ai/hailo-rpi5-examples)

Welcome to the Hailo Raspberry Pi 5 Examples repository. This project showcases various community projects and examples demonstrating the capabilities of the Hailo AI processor. These examples will help you get started with AI on embedded devices.
The examples in this repository are designed to work with the Raspberry Pi AI Kit and AI HAT, and x86_64 Ubuntu machine supporting both the Hailo8 (26 TOPS) and Hailo8L (13 TOPS) AI processors.
Visit the [Hailo Official Website](https://hailo.ai/) and [Hailo Community Forum](https://community.hailo.ai/) for more information.

## Hailo Apps Infra Repository
Hailo's official examples and pipelines are available in the [Hailo Apps Infra repo](https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo-apps-infra) repository.
See the Hailo Apps Infra repo for more information and documentation on how to use the pipelines and development guide.

## Install Hailo Hardware and Software Setup on Raspberry Pi

For instructions on how to set up Hailo's hardware and software on the Raspberry Pi 5, see the [Hailo Raspberry Pi 5 installation guide](doc/install-raspberry-pi5.md#how-to-set-up-raspberry-pi-5-and-hailo).

# Hailo RPi5 Basic Pipelines
The basic pipelines examples demonstrate object detection, human pose estimation, and instance segmentation, providing a solid foundation for your own projects.
This repo is using our new [Hailo Apps Infra](https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo-apps-infra) repo as a dependency.
See our Developement Guide for more information on how to use the pipelines to create your own custom pipelines.

## Installation

### Clone the Repository
```bash
git clone https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo-rpi5-examples.git
```
Navigate to the repository directory:
```bash
cd hailo-rpi5-examples
```

### Installation
Run the following script to automate the installation process:
```bash
./install.sh
```

### Documentation
For additional information and documentation on how to use the pipelines to create your own custom pipelines, see the [Basic Pipelines Documentation](doc/basic-pipelines.md).

### Running The Examples
When opening a new terminal session, ensure you have sourced the environment setup script:
```bash
source setup_env.sh
```
### Detection Example
For more information see [Detection Example Documentation.](doc/basic-pipelines.md#detection-example)

![Detection Example](doc/images/detection.gif)

#### Run the simple detection example:
```bash
python basic_pipelines/detection_simple.py
```
To close the application, press `Ctrl+C`.

This is lightweight version of the detection example, mainly focusing on demonstrating Hailo performance while minimizing CPU load. The internal GStreamer video processing pipeline is simplified by minimizing video processing tasks, and the YOLOv6 Nano model is used.

#### Run the full detection example:
This is the full detection example, including object tracker and multiple video resolution support - see more information [Detection Example Documentation](doc/basic-pipelines.md#detection-example):

```bash
python basic_pipelines/detection.py
```
To close the application, press `Ctrl+C`.

#### Running with Raspberry Pi Camera input:
```bash
python basic_pipelines/detection.py --input rpi
```

#### Running with USB camera input (webcam):
There are 2 ways:

Specify the argument `--input` to `usb`:
```bash
python basic_pipelines/detection.py --input usb
```

This will automatically detect the available USB camera (if multiple are connected, it will use the first detected).

Second way:

Detect the available camera using this script:
```bash
get-usb-camera
```
Run example using USB camera input - Use the device found by the previous script:
```bash
python basic_pipelines/detection.py --input /dev/video<X>
```

For additional options, execute:
```bash
python basic_pipelines/detection.py --help
```

#### Retrained Networks Support
The retrain guide is available in the [Hailo Apps Infra repo: Retraining Example](https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo-apps-infra/blob/main/doc/developer_guide/retraining_example.md).

### Pose Estimation Example
For more information see [Pose Estimation Example Documentation.](doc/basic-pipelines.md#pose-estimation-example)

![Pose Estimation Example](doc/images/pose_estimation.gif)

# Additional Examples and Resources

## Hailo Apps Infra
Hailo RPi5 Examples are using the [Hailo Apps Infra Repository](https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo-apps-infra) as a dependency. The Hailo Apps Infra repository contains the infrastructure of Hailo applications and pipelines.
It is aimed for to provide tools for developers who want to create their own custom pipelines and applications. It features a simple and easy-to-use API for creating custom pipelines and applications.
It it installed as a pip package and can be used as a dependency in your own projects. See more information in its documentation and Development Guide.

### CLIP Application

CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) predicts the most relevant text prompt on real-time video frames using Hailo8/8l AI processor.
See the [hailo-CLIP Repository](https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo-CLIP) for more information.
Click the image below to watch the demo on YouTube.

[![Watch the demo on YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/XXizBHtCLew/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/XXizBHtCLew)


#### Frigate Integration

Frigate is an open-source video surveillance software that runs on a Raspberry Pi.
Hailo is officially integrated into Frigate framework starting from version 0.16.0.
See [Hailo Official Integration with Frigate](https://community.hailo.ai/t/hailo-official-integration-with-frigate/13679) for more information.


### Raspberry Pi Official Examples

#### rpicam-apps

Raspberry Pi [rpicam-apps](https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/camera_software.html#rpicam-apps) Hailo post-processing examples.
This is Raspberry Pi's official example for AI post-processing using the Hailo AI processor integrated into their CPP camera framework.
The documentation on how to use rpicam-apps can be found [here](https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/ai.html).

#### picamera2

Raspberry Pi [picamera2](https://github.com/raspberrypi/picamera2) is the libcamera-based replacement for Picamera, which was a Python interface to the Raspberry Pi's legacy camera stack. Picamera2 also presents an easy-to-use Python API.

## Additional Resources

### Hailo Python API
The Hailo Python API is now available on the Raspberry Pi 5. This API allows you to run inference on the Hailo-8L AI processor using Python.
For examples, see our [Python code examples](https://github.com/hailo-ai/Hailo-Application-Code-Examples/tree/main/runtime/python).
Additional examples can be found in RPi [picamera2](#picamera2) code.
Visit our [HailoRT Python API documentation](https://hailo.ai/developer-zone/documentation/hailort-v4-18-0/?page=api%2Fpython_api.html#module-hailo_platform.drivers) for more information.

### Hailo Dataflow Compiler (DFC)

The Hailo Dataflow Compiler (DFC) is a software tool that enables developers to compile their neural networks to run on the Hailo-8/8L AI processors.
The DFC is available for download from the [Hailo Developer Zone](https://hailo.ai/developer-zone/software-downloads/) (Registration required).
For examples, tutorials, and retrain instructions, see the [Hailo Model Zoo Repo](https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo_model_zoo).
Additional documentation and [tutorials](https://hailo.ai/developer-zone/documentation/dataflow-compiler/latest/?sp_referrer=tutorials/tutorials.html) can be found in the [Hailo Developer Zone Documentation](https://hailo.ai/developer-zone/documentation/).
For a full end-to-end training and deployment example, see the [Hailo Apps Infra repo: Retraining Example](https://github.com/hailo-ai/hailo-apps-infra/blob/main/doc/developer_guide/retraining_example.md).

from pathlib import Path
import sys

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
project_root_str = str(PROJECT_ROOT)
if project_root_str in sys.path:
    sys.path.remove(project_root_str)
sys.path.insert(0, project_root_str)

import gi
gi.require_version('Gst', '1.0')
from gi.repository import Gst
import os
import select
import shlex
import subprocess
import threading
import time
from collections import deque
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

import cv2
import hailo

try:
    import termios
    import tty
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - platform dependent
    termios = None
    tty = None

from config.settings import (
    get_settings,
    CONFIRMED_MIN_CONFIDENCE,
    POTHOLE_LABELS,
    TRAINING_DATA_ENABLED,
    TRAINING_DATA_MIN_CONFIDENCE,
    UPLOAD_JPEG_QUALITY,
)
from core.recorder import FfmpegRecorder

from detection.local_saver import LocalDetectionSaver

from hailo_apps.hailo_app_python.core.common.buffer_utils import get_caps_from_pad, get_numpy_from_buffer
from hailo_apps.hailo_app_python.core.gstreamer.gstreamer_app import app_callback_class
from basic_pipelines.robolyze_detection_app import RobolyzeDetectionApp

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# User-defined class to be used in the callback function
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inheritance from the app_callback_class
class user_app_callback_class(app_callback_class):
    def __init__(
        self,
        label_filter: LabelFilter,
        visualizer: FrameVisualizer,
        uploader: UploadPipeline,
        gps_reader,
        logger,
        local_save_pipeline: Optional[LocalSavePipeline] = None,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self._frame_times = deque(maxlen=60)  # keeps timestamps for FPS calculation
        self.fps = 0.0
        self.label_filter = label_filter
        self.visualizer = visualizer
        self.uploader = uploader
        self.gps_reader = gps_reader
        self.logger = logger
        self.local_save_pipeline = local_save_pipeline
        self.use_frame = True
        self.ui_frame_from_pipeline = False
        self._last_gps_warn_at = 0.0
        self._warned_local_save_error = False

    def update_fps(self):
        """Update FPS using a sliding window over the last N callback timestamps.

        Measures end-to-end pipeline throughput: frames that completed the full
        source → decode → inference → tracker → callback chain per second.
        """
        now = time.time()
        self._frame_times.append(now)
        if len(self._frame_times) >= 2:
            elapsed = self._frame_times[-1] - self._frame_times[0]
            if elapsed > 0:
                self.fps = (len(self._frame_times) - 1) / elapsed

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# User-defined callback function
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _is_confirmed(det: Dict) -> bool:
    conf = det.get("confidence", 0.0)
    if normalize_label(det.get("class_name")) in POTHOLE_LABELS:
        return conf >= TRAINING_DATA_MIN_CONFIDENCE
    return conf >= CONFIRMED_MIN_CONFIDENCE


# This is the callback function that will be called when data is available from the pipeline
def _parse_hailo_detections(
    detections, width: Optional[int], height: Optional[int]
) -> List[Dict]:
    if width is None or height is None:
        return []

    parsed: List[Dict] = []
    for detection in detections:
        label = detection.get_label()
        class_id = getattr(detection, "get_class_id", lambda: None)()
        if label in (None, "", " "):
            label = f"class_{class_id}" if class_id is not None else "unknown"
        bbox = detection.get_bbox()
        if bbox is None:
            continue
        confidence = detection.get_confidence()

        x1 = bbox.xmin() * width
        y1 = bbox.ymin() * height
        x2 = bbox.xmax() * width
        y2 = bbox.ymax() * height

        entry: Dict = {
            "class_name": label,
            "confidence": float(confidence) if confidence is not None else 0.0,
            "bbox": [x1, y1, x2, y2],
        }

        track = detection.get_objects_typed(hailo.HAILO_UNIQUE_ID)
        if len(track) == 1:
            entry["track_id"] = int(track[0].get_id())

        parsed.append(entry)

    return parsed


def app_callback(pad, info, user_data):
    # Get the GstBuffer from the probe info
    buffer = info.get_buffer()
    # Check if the buffer is valid
    if buffer is None:
        return Gst.PadProbeReturn.OK

    # Using the user_data to count the number of frames
    user_data.increment()
    user_data.update_fps()

    # Unconditional frame heartbeat — fires every ~5s regardless of detections so
    # we can distinguish "no defects in view" from "pipeline frozen" in the logs.
    now_hb = time.monotonic()
    if now_hb - getattr(user_data, "_last_frame_hb_at", 0.0) >= 5.0:
        user_data.logger.info(
            "Frame heartbeat frame=%s fps=%.2f",
            user_data.get_count(),
            user_data.fps,
        )
        user_data._last_frame_hb_at = now_hb

    # Get the caps from the pad
    format, width, height = get_caps_from_pad(pad)

    # Get the detections from the buffer
    roi = hailo.get_roi_from_buffer(buffer)
    detections = roi.get_objects_typed(hailo.HAILO_DETECTION)

    parsed_detections = _parse_hailo_detections(detections, width, height)
    filtered_detections = user_data.label_filter.filter(parsed_detections)

    # Split into confirmed and training tiers. See _is_confirmed for the
    # per-class threshold rules (pothole uses the lower training floor so the
    # dashboard sees low-confidence potholes too).
    confirmed_detections: List[Dict] = []
    training_detections: List[Dict] = []
    for det in filtered_detections:
        if _is_confirmed(det):
            confirmed_detections.append(det)
        elif TRAINING_DATA_ENABLED:
            training_detections.append(det)

    detection_count = len(confirmed_detections)

    # GPS — attach to both confirmed and training detections when a fix is available.
    # Training metadata records gps_fix=false with a LOCATION fallback when no fix.
    gps_fix = None
    if (confirmed_detections or training_detections) and getattr(user_data, "gps_reader", None) is not None:
        try:
            gps_fix = user_data.gps_reader.get_fix(
                require_valid=True,
                allow_stale=False,
            )
            if gps_fix is None:
                gps_fix = user_data.gps_reader.get_fix(
                    require_valid=True,
                    allow_stale=True,
                )
        except Exception:
            gps_fix = None

        if gps_fix is not None:
            lat, lon = gps_fix
            for detection in confirmed_detections:
                detection["gps"] = {"lat": lat, "lon": lon}
            for detection in training_detections:
                detection["gps"] = {"lat": lat, "lon": lon}
        else:
            # Avoid spamming logs when GPS is initializing / temporarily unavailable.
            now = time.time()
            if now - getattr(user_data, "_last_gps_warn_at", 0.0) >= 5.0:
                user_data.logger.warning(
                    "No GPS fix available; sending payloads without GPS (set GPS_* in .env)"
                )
                user_data._last_gps_warn_at = now

    # We might not be displaying frames, but we still need the frame bytes for uploads.
    any_detections = confirmed_detections or training_detections
    want_frame = bool(any_detections) or bool(user_data.use_frame)
    frame = None
    if want_frame and format is not None and width is not None and height is not None:
        frame = get_numpy_from_buffer(buffer, format, width, height)

    if frame is not None:
        # Convert RGB→BGR once; all downstream consumers (local save, upload,
        # UI set_frame) expect BGR.
        frame_bgr = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)

        if confirmed_detections and user_data.local_save_pipeline is not None:
            try:
                # Local saver runs async on its own queue, so it needs an
                # independent buffer (frame_bgr is about to be handed to the
                # uploader as raw — keep it untouched here).
                user_data.local_save_pipeline.process_frame(
                    frame_bgr.copy(), confirmed_detections
                )
            except Exception as exc:
                if not user_data._warned_local_save_error:
                    user_data.logger.warning(
                        "Local detection save disabled due to error: %s", exc
                    )
                    user_data._warned_local_save_error = True
                    user_data.local_save_pipeline = None

        # Tkinter UI preview: draw on a *separate* copy so the uploader's raw
        # frame stays clean. Skipped entirely when no UI is consuming frames.
        if user_data.use_frame and not user_data.ui_frame_from_pipeline:
            ui_frame = frame_bgr.copy()
            user_data.visualizer.draw(ui_frame, confirmed_detections, inplace=True)
            cv2.putText(
                ui_frame,
                f"Detections: {detection_count}",
                (10, 30),
                cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1, (0, 255, 0), 2,
            )
            cv2.putText(
                ui_frame,
                f"FPS: {user_data.fps:.2f}",
                (10, 60),
                cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1, (0, 255, 255), 2,
            )
            user_data.set_frame(ui_frame)

        frame_w = width or 0
        frame_h = height or 0

        # Confirmed tier: pass raw frame only; the upload worker renders the
        # labelled copy off-thread (cv2.copy/draw/putText no longer block the
        # GStreamer streaming thread).
        if confirmed_detections:
            user_data.uploader.process_frame(
                None, frame_bgr, confirmed_detections,
                user_data.get_count(), frame_w, frame_h,
                fps=user_data.fps,
                detection_count=detection_count,
            )

        # Training tier: raw frame + YOLO labels + metadata to S3 only
        if training_detections:
            user_data.uploader.process_training_frame(
                frame_bgr, training_detections,
                user_data.get_count(), frame_w, frame_h,
            )
    elif any_detections:
        # Detections exist but we couldn't pull the frame out of the buffer.
        # Log once per run to avoid spamming.
        if not getattr(user_data, "_warned_no_frame", False):
            user_data.logger.warning(
                "Detections present but frame unavailable; uploads disabled. "
                "format=%s width=%s height=%s",
                format,
                width,
                height,
            )
            user_data._warned_no_frame = True

    return Gst.PadProbeReturn.OK

def _get_cli_arg(argv, name):
    if name in argv:
        idx = argv.index(name)
        if idx + 1 < len(argv):
            return argv[idx + 1]
    prefix = f"{name}="
    for arg in argv:
        if arg.startswith(prefix):
            return arg.split("=", 1)[1]
    return None


def _parse_env_float(name: str, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    value = os.getenv(name)
    if value is None:
        return default
    try:
        return max(0.0, float(value))
    except ValueError:
        return default


def _wait_for_first_gps_fix(gps_reader, logger, timeout_sec: float) -> None:
    timeout_sec = max(0.0, timeout_sec)
    if gps_reader is None or timeout_sec <= 0:
        return

    logger.info(
        "GPS warm-up: waiting up to %.0fs for first valid fix", timeout_sec
    )
    deadline = time.time() + timeout_sec
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            fix = gps_reader.get_fix(require_valid=True, allow_stale=True)
        except Exception:
            fix = None
        if fix is not None:
            lat, lon = fix
            logger.info(
                "GPS warm-up: fix acquired lat=%.6f lon=%.6f",
                lat,
                lon,
            )
            return
        time.sleep(1.0)

    logger.warning(
        "GPS warm-up: no valid fix within %.0fs; continuing without GPS until lock",
        timeout_sec,
    )


def _run_poweroff(command: str, logger) -> None:
    command = (command or "").strip()
    if not command:
        logger.warning("Shutdown requested but UI_POWEROFF_CMD is empty; skipping poweroff")
        return

    logger.warning("Executing poweroff command: %s", command)
    try:
        args = shlex.split(command)
    except ValueError as exc:
        logger.error("Invalid poweroff command in UI_POWEROFF_CMD: %s", exc)
        return

    try:
        result = subprocess.run(args, check=False)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        logger.error("Poweroff command failed: %s", exc)
        return
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error("Poweroff command failed: %s", exc)
        return

    if result.returncode != 0:
        logger.error("Poweroff command exited with code %s", result.returncode)


class _EscStopListener:
    def __init__(self, *, enabled: bool, logger, on_escape) -> None:
        self._enabled = bool(enabled)
        self._logger = logger
        self._on_escape = on_escape
        self._thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None
        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
        self._fd: Optional[int] = None
        self._original_term_attrs = None
        self._active = False

    def start(self) -> None:
        if not self._enabled:
            return
        if termios is None or tty is None:
            self._logger.warning("ESC stop disabled: terminal control modules unavailable")
            return
        if not sys.stdin.isatty():
            self._logger.warning("ESC stop disabled: stdin is not a TTY")
            return

        try:
            fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
            original_attrs = termios.tcgetattr(fd)
            tty.setcbreak(fd)
        except Exception as exc:
            self._logger.warning("ESC stop disabled: cannot set terminal cbreak mode (%s)", exc)
            return

        self._fd = fd
        self._original_term_attrs = original_attrs
        self._active = True
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._listen_loop, name="esc-stop-listener", daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()
        self._logger.info("ESC stop listener enabled (UI disabled mode)")

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop_event.set()
        if self._thread is not None:
            self._thread.join(timeout=0.5)
            self._thread = None
        self._restore_terminal()

    def _restore_terminal(self) -> None:
        if not self._active:
            return
        self._active = False
        if self._fd is None or self._original_term_attrs is None:
            return
        try:
            termios.tcsetattr(self._fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, self._original_term_attrs)
        except Exception as exc:
            self._logger.warning("Failed to restore terminal mode after ESC listener: %s", exc)
        finally:
            self._fd = None
            self._original_term_attrs = None

    def _listen_loop(self) -> None:
        fd = self._fd
        if fd is None:
            return
        try:
            while not self._stop_event.is_set():
                try:
                    ready, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if not ready:
                    continue

                try:
                    key = os.read(fd, 1)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if key != b"\x1b":
                    continue

                # Ignore escape sequences (e.g. arrow keys) and only react to a plain ESC press.
                try:
                    extra_ready, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.03)
                except Exception:
                    extra_ready = []
                if extra_ready:
                    try:
                        os.read(fd, 16)
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                    continue

                self._logger.warning("ESC pressed; requesting graceful shutdown")
                try:
                    self._on_escape()
                except Exception as exc:
                    self._logger.error("Failed to request shutdown from ESC listener: %s", exc)
                break
        finally:
            self._restore_terminal()


def _flush_uploader_with_timeout(uploader: UploadPipeline, logger, timeout_sec: float) -> None:
    timeout_sec = max(0.0, float(timeout_sec))
    if timeout_sec <= 0:
        try:
            uploader.flush()
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("Uploader flush failed during shutdown: %s", exc)
        return

    state = {"done": False, "exc": None}

    def _worker():
        try:
            uploader.flush()
        except Exception as exc:
            state["exc"] = exc
        finally:
            state["done"] = True

    worker = threading.Thread(target=_worker, name="uploader-flush", daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    worker.join(timeout=timeout_sec)
    if not state["done"]:
        logger.warning(
            "Uploader flush exceeded %.1fs during stop; continuing shutdown", timeout_sec
        )
        return
    if state["exc"] is not None:
        logger.warning("Uploader flush failed during shutdown: %s", state["exc"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    project_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    env_file     = project_root / ".env"
    env_path_str = str(env_file)

                settings.save_detections_root,
                settings.save_detections_queue_size,
                settings.save_detections_jpeg_quality,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Failed to initialize local detection saver: %s", exc)

    user_data = user_app_callback_class(
        label_filter,
        visualizer,
        uploader,
        gps_reader,
        logger,
        local_save_pipeline=local_save_pipeline,
    )
    combined_ui_mode = settings.shutdown_ui_enabled and is_shutdown_ui_supported(logger)
    app = RobolyzeDetectionApp(
        app_callback, user_data, combined_ui_mode=combined_ui_mode
    )
    if not combined_ui_mode:
        # When no display environment is available (e.g. running as a systemd service),
        # autovideosink tries to use KMS/DRM and fails with "Permission denied".
        # Fall back to fakesink so the pipeline runs purely headless.
        import os
        if not os.environ.get("DISPLAY") and not os.environ.get("WAYLAND_DISPLAY"):
            app.video_sink = "fakesink"
    if combined_ui_mode:
        # In UI mode, preview frames come from the post-overlay pipeline tap.
        user_data.ui_frame_from_pipeline = True
    shutdown_ui = create_shutdown_ui(
        enabled=combined_ui_mode,
        logger=logger,
        on_shutdown_request=app.request_shutdown,
        show_stop_button=settings.shutdown_ui_stop_button_enabled,
        show_poweroff_button=settings.shutdown_ui_poweroff_button_enabled,
        frame_provider=user_data.get_frame if combined_ui_mode else None,
        frame_is_rgb=combined_ui_mode,
    )
    esc_listener = _EscStopListener(
        enabled=(not combined_ui_mode and settings.esc_stop_enabled),
        logger=logger,
        on_escape=app.request_shutdown,
    )
    esc_listener.start()

    recorder = None
    if settings.record_enabled:
        if not input_arg:
            print("RECORD=1 but no --input/RTSP_URL provided. Recording disabled.")
        elif not input_arg.lower().startswith("rtsp"):
            print("RECORD=1 but input is not RTSP. Recording disabled.")

                output_path=settings.record_path,
                ffmpeg_path=settings.ffmpeg_path,
            )
            try:
                recorder.start()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                print("Recording disabled: ffmpeg not found in PATH.")
                recorder = None
            else:
                if recorder.is_running():
                    print(f"Recording enabled: {recorder.output_pattern}")
                else:
                    print(f"Recording failed to start. See {recorder.log_path} for details.")
                    recorder = None

    system_exit_error = None
    runtime_error = None
    try:
        app.run()
    except SystemExit as exc:
        system_exit_error = exc
    except Exception as exc:
        runtime_error = exc
    finally:
        esc_listener.stop()
        stop_requested = shutdown_ui.was_stop_requested()
        # Close UI first so Stop behaves like Ctrl+C from the user's perspective.
        shutdown_ui.stop()
        if recorder:
            recorder.stop()
        if gps_reader is not None:
            gps_reader.close()
        if local_save_pipeline is not None:
            local_save_pipeline.close()
        if stop_requested:
            stop_flush_timeout_sec = _parse_env_float("STOP_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SEC", 3.0)
            _flush_uploader_with_timeout(uploader, logger, stop_flush_timeout_sec)
        else:
            uploader.flush()

    if shutdown_ui.was_shutdown_requested():
        if settings.shutdown_ui_poweroff_enabled:
            _run_poweroff(settings.shutdown_ui_poweroff_cmd, logger)
        else:
            logger.info("Shutdown requested from UI, but poweroff is disabled")
    elif shutdown_ui.was_stop_requested():
        logger.info("Stop requested from UI; application stopped without poweroff")

    if runtime_error is not None:
        raise runtime_error
    if system_exit_error is not None:
        raise system_exit_error

=== /home/rasp/miniproj_epan/hailo-rpi5-examples/utils/calibrate_blur.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score sample images so a BLUR_THRESHOLD can be picked from real footage.

Not a pytest test -- this prints numbers for a human to read. Point it at a
folder of images; if the blurred and sharp samples are separated into
subfolders it also sweeps thresholds and suggests a cut point.

    # labelled: subfolders detected by name (blur*/rain* vs sharp*/clear*/non*)
    python utils/calibrate_blur.py samples/

    # labelled: explicit folders
    python utils/calibrate_blur.py --blur-dir samples/rain --sharp-dir samples/dry

    # unlabelled: just dump a score per image
    python utils/calibrate_blur.py samples/

Compare ROIs to see whether excluding sky/background separates the classes
better than the full frame:

    python utils/calibrate_blur.py samples/ --roi 0.15,0.45,0.85,0.95
    python utils/calibrate_blur.py samples/ --roi full
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

import cv2

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from detection.blur import FULL_FRAME_ROI, Roi, crop_to_roi  # noqa: E402

_IMAGE_SUFFIXES = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".webp"}

# Substrings used to guess which subfolder holds which class.
_BLUR_HINTS = ("blur", "rain", "wet", "bad")
_SHARP_HINTS = ("sharp", "clear", "dry", "non", "clean", "good")

# Default road-surface ROI for the rear-top-mounted camera: bottom-centre.
# Measured across 152 production frames (all 1920x1080): they are pillarboxed
# with real content spanning x 0.110-0.888, and the red truck body reaches as
# high as y 0.806. The bounds below stay inside the content and stop above the
# body -- the body is bolted to the camera so it never blurs, and scoring it
# would mask real blur.
_DEFAULT_ROI: Roi = (0.15, 0.45, 0.85, 0.80)


def _laplacian_score(frame, roi: Roi) -> float:
    region = crop_to_roi(frame, roi)
    if region.ndim == 3:
        region = cv2.cvtColor(region, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    return float(cv2.Laplacian(region, cv2.CV_64F).var())


def _iter_images(directory: Path) -> List[Path]:
    return sorted(
        path for path in directory.rglob("*")
        if path.suffix.lower() in _IMAGE_SUFFIXES
    )


def _score_dir(directory: Path, roi: Roi) -> List[Tuple[Path, float]]:
    scored: List[Tuple[Path, float]] = []
    for path in _iter_images(directory):
        frame = cv2.imread(str(path))
        if frame is None:
            print(f"  !! unreadable, skipped: {path}")
            continue
        scored.append((path, _laplacian_score(frame, roi)))
    return scored


def _guess_class_dirs(root: Path) -> Tuple[Optional[Path], Optional[Path]]:
    """Find blur/sharp subfolders by name; (None, None) if not conclusive."""
    blur_dir = sharp_dir = None
    for child in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        name = child.name.lower()
        if blur_dir is None and any(h in name for h in _BLUR_HINTS):
            blur_dir = child
        elif sharp_dir is None and any(h in name for h in _SHARP_HINTS):
            sharp_dir = child
    return blur_dir, sharp_dir


def _print_scores(title: str, scored: Sequence[Tuple[Path, float]]) -> None:
    print(f"\n{title}  (n={len(scored)})")
    print("-" * 72)
    for path, score in sorted(scored, key=lambda item: item[1]):
        print(f"  {score:12.2f}   {path.name}")
    if scored:
        values = [s for _, s in scored]
        values_sorted = sorted(values)
        median = values_sorted[len(values_sorted) // 2]
        print(
            f"  min={min(values):.2f}  median={median:.2f}  max={max(values):.2f}"
        )


def _sweep(blur: Sequence[float], sharp: Sequence[float]) -> None:
    """Report the threshold that best separates the two labelled classes."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 72)
    print("THRESHOLD SWEEP   (predicted blur when score < threshold)")
    print("=" * 72)

    candidates = sorted(set(blur) | set(sharp))
    midpoints = [
        (a + b) / 2 for a, b in zip(candidates, candidates[1:])
    ] or candidates
    best = None
    for threshold in midpoints:
        true_pos = sum(1 for s in blur if s < threshold)
        true_neg = sum(1 for s in sharp if s >= threshold)
        accuracy = (true_pos + true_neg) / (len(blur) + len(sharp))
        if best is None or accuracy > best[1]:
            best = (threshold, accuracy, true_pos, true_neg)

    threshold, accuracy, true_pos, true_neg = best
    false_neg = len(blur) - true_pos
    false_pos = len(sharp) - true_neg
    print(f"  best threshold : {threshold:.2f}")
    print(f"  accuracy       : {accuracy * 100:.1f}%")
    print(f"  blurred  caught: {true_pos}/{len(blur)}   (missed {false_neg})")
    print(f"  sharp    kept  : {true_neg}/{len(sharp)}  (mis-flagged {false_pos})")

    # Separation margin: if the classes do not overlap, any threshold in the gap
    # works and the signal is trustworthy. Overlap means Laplacian variance
    # alone cannot cleanly split this footage.
    max_blur = max(blur)
    min_sharp = min(sharp)
    print()
    if max_blur < min_sharp:
        print(
            f"  CLEAN SEPARATION: blurred max ({max_blur:.2f}) < sharp min "
            f"({min_sharp:.2f})."
        )
        print(
            f"  Any threshold in ({max_blur:.2f}, {min_sharp:.2f}) separates "
            f"the samples; midpoint {(max_blur + min_sharp) / 2:.2f} is the "
            f"safest pick."
        )
    else:
        print(
            f"  OVERLAP: blurred max ({max_blur:.2f}) >= sharp min "
            f"({min_sharp:.2f})."
        )
        print(
            "  No threshold separates these samples perfectly. The blur flag is"
            " advisory, so some error is tolerable -- but if the overlap is"
            " wide, Laplacian variance is not capturing rain blur on this"
            " footage and a v2 method is worth considering."
        )
    print(
        f"\n  Set in .env:  BLUR_THRESHOLD={threshold:.1f}"
    )


def _parse_roi(value: str) -> Roi:
    if value.strip().lower() == "full":
        return FULL_FRAME_ROI
    parts = [p.strip() for p in value.split(",")]
    if len(parts) != 4:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            "ROI must be 'full' or four comma-separated fractions "
            "x0,y0,x1,y1 (e.g. 0.15,0.45,0.85,0.95)"
        )
    try:
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = (float(p) for p in parts)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ROI values must be numbers")
    if not all(0.0 <= v <= 1.0 for v in (x0, y0, x1, y1)):
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ROI fractions must be within 0.0-1.0")
    if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ROI must satisfy x0<x1 and y0<y1")
    return (x0, y0, x1, y1)


def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Score sample images to calibrate BLUR_THRESHOLD.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "root", nargs="?", type=Path,
        help="Folder of images. Blur/sharp subfolders are auto-detected.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--blur-dir", type=Path, help="Folder of blurred samples")
    parser.add_argument("--sharp-dir", type=Path, help="Folder of sharp samples")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--roi", type=_parse_roi, default=_DEFAULT_ROI,
        help="Road ROI as x0,y0,x1,y1 fractions, or 'full'. "
             "Default: %s" % (",".join(str(v) for v in _DEFAULT_ROI),),
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    blur_dir, sharp_dir = args.blur_dir, args.sharp_dir
    if blur_dir is None and sharp_dir is None and args.root is not None:
        if not args.root.is_dir():
            parser.error(f"not a directory: {args.root}")
        blur_dir, sharp_dir = _guess_class_dirs(args.root)

    if blur_dir is None and sharp_dir is None and args.root is None:
        parser.error("give a root folder, or --blur-dir and --sharp-dir")

    roi = args.roi
    print(f"ROI (x0,y0,x1,y1 fractions): {roi}")
    print("Score = variance of Laplacian over the ROI. Higher = sharper.")

    if blur_dir is not None and sharp_dir is not None:
        for directory in (blur_dir, sharp_dir):
            if not directory.is_dir():
                parser.error(f"not a directory: {directory}")
        blur_scored = _score_dir(blur_dir, roi)
        sharp_scored = _score_dir(sharp_dir, roi)
        _print_scores(f"BLURRED  [{blur_dir}]", blur_scored)
        _print_scores(f"SHARP    [{sharp_dir}]", sharp_scored)
        if not blur_scored or not sharp_scored:
            print("\nNeed readable images in both folders to sweep a threshold.")
            return 1
        _sweep([s for _, s in blur_scored], [s for _, s in sharp_scored])
        return 0

    # Unlabelled: dump scores only. A threshold needs both classes.
    scored = _score_dir(args.root, roi)
    if not scored:
        print(f"\nNo readable images found under {args.root}")
        return 1
    _print_scores(f"ALL IMAGES  [{args.root}]", scored)
    print(
        "\nUnlabelled run: scores only. Separate the samples into blur/ and"
        " sharp/ subfolders (or pass --blur-dir/--sharp-dir) to get a"
        " threshold suggestion."
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Directory helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os


def ensure_directories(*paths: str) -> None:
    """Create directories if they do not exist."""
    for path in paths:
        if path:
            os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)

=== /home/rasp/miniproj_epan/hailo-rpi5-examples/utils/gps.py ===
"""GPS reader utilities (optional).

This module is designed to be safe to import even when GPS dependencies
(`pyserial`, `pynmea2`) are not installed. GPS is enabled via env vars:

- GPS_ENABLED=1
- GPS_PORT=/dev/ttyACM0
- GPS_BAUD=9600
- GPS_FIX_MAX_AGE_SEC=2

A lightweight daemon thread reads NMEA sentences from the serial port and
caches the latest fix.  get_fix() returns from cache instantly — it never
touches the serial port or blocks the caller.

No file locks.  No status files.  Multiple processes can open the same
serial port independently (Linux CDC-ACM delivers data to all readers).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
import os
import threading
import time
from typing import Any, Optional, Tuple


def _parse_bool(value: Optional[str], default: bool = False) -> bool:
    if value is None:
        return default
    normalized = value.strip().lower()
    if normalized in {"1", "true", "yes", "y", "on"}:
        return True
    if normalized in {"0", "false", "no", "n", "off"}:
        return False
    return default


def _parse_int(value: Optional[str], default: int) -> int:
    if value is None:
        return default
    try:
        return int(value)
    except ValueError:
        return default


def _parse_float(value: Optional[str], default: float) -> float:
    if value is None:
        return default
    try:
        return float(value)
    except ValueError:
        return default


_KNOTS_TO_KMH = 1.852


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GpsFix:
    lat: float
    lon: float
    ts: float
    valid: bool
    speed_kmh: float = 0.0

    @property
    def age_sec(self) -> float:
        return max(0.0, time.time() - self.ts)


class GPSReader:
    """GPS reader: background serial thread + instant cache reads.

    A daemon thread reads NMEA sentences (blocking readline, timeout=1)
    and caches the latest parsed fix.  get_fix() reads from cache only —
    it never touches the serial port and returns in microseconds.

    No file locks, no status files.  The serial port is opened without
    fcntl.flock so multiple processes can coexist on the same device.
    """

    _NMEA_PREFIXES = ("$GPRMC", "$GPGGA", "$GNRMC", "$GNGGA")

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        port: str,
        baud: int,
        max_age_sec: float,
        logger: Any,
        serial_module: Any,
        nmea_module: Any,
    ) -> None:
        self._logger = logger
        self._nmea = nmea_module
        self._max_age_sec = max(0.0, float(max_age_sec))

        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._latest: Optional[GpsFix] = None
        self._last_valid: Optional[GpsFix] = None
        self._last_speed_kmh: float = 0.0
        self._last_speed_ts: float = 0.0
        self._stop = threading.Event()

        # timeout=1 is required for CDC-ACM USB serial on this kernel;
        # timeout=0 / select / small timeouts silently return no data.
        self._serial = serial_module.Serial(port, baud, timeout=1)
        try:
            self._serial.reset_input_buffer()
        except Exception:
            pass
        self._save_config_to_flash()

        self._thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self._run, daemon=True, name="GPSReader"
        )
        self._thread.start()
        logger.info(
            "GPS started port=%s baud=%s max_age=%.1fs",
            port, baud, self._max_age_sec,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API  (instant, never blocks)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_fix(
        self,
        *,
        require_valid: bool = True,
        allow_stale: bool = False,
    ) -> Optional[Tuple[float, float]]:
        with self._lock:
            fix = self._latest
            last_valid = self._last_valid

        if fix is not None and fix.valid and fix.age_sec <= self._max_age_sec:
            return (fix.lat, fix.lon)

        # Fresh fix unavailable — fall back to last known valid position.
        # On a vehicle this is always better than returning nothing.
        if allow_stale and last_valid is not None:
            return (last_valid.lat, last_valid.lon)

        if fix is None:
            return None
        if require_valid and not fix.valid:
            return None
        if not allow_stale and fix.age_sec > self._max_age_sec:
            return None
        return (fix.lat, fix.lon)

    def get_speed(self) -> Optional[float]:
        """Return current speed in km/h, or None if no valid fix available."""
        with self._lock:
            fix = self._latest
        if fix is None or not fix.valid or fix.age_sec > self._max_age_sec:
            return None
        return fix.speed_kmh

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()
        try:
            self._thread.join(timeout=2)
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            self._serial.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        self._logger.info("GPS stopped")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # UBX helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _build_ubx(self, cls: int, id_: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        length = len(payload)
        msg = bytes([cls, id_, length & 0xFF, (length >> 8) & 0xFF]) + payload
        ck_a = ck_b = 0
        for b in msg:
            ck_a = (ck_a + b) & 0xFF
            ck_b = (ck_b + ck_a) & 0xFF
        return b'\xB5\x62' + msg + bytes([ck_a, ck_b])

    def _save_config_to_flash(self) -> None:
        """Send UBX-CFG-CFG to persist GPS configuration to internal flash.

        Saves port settings, nav config, and message rates so they survive
        power cycles without needing battery backup.  This allows warm start
        on short reboots (if the module's supercap retains BBR almanac data).

        Note: does NOT save almanac/ephemeris — that requires hardware V_BCKP.
        """
        payload = bytes([
            0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # clearMask: clear nothing
            0x1F, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # saveMask: ioPort|msgConf|infMsg|navConf|rxmConf
            0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # loadMask: load nothing
            0x02,                    # deviceMask: internal flash
        ])
        try:
            self._serial.write(self._build_ubx(0x06, 0x09, payload))
            self._serial.flush()
            self._logger.debug("GPS config saved to flash")
        except Exception:
            pass

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Background thread
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _run(self) -> None:
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            try:
                raw = self._serial.readline()
                if not raw:
                    continue
                line = raw.decode("ascii", errors="ignore").strip()
                if not line or not line.startswith(self._NMEA_PREFIXES):
                    continue

                try:
                    msg = self._nmea.parse(line, check=True)
                except Exception:
                    continue

                lat = getattr(msg, "latitude", None)
                lon = getattr(msg, "longitude", None)
                if lat is None or lon is None:
                    continue

                lat_f = float(lat)
                lon_f = float(lon)

                valid = True
                speed_kmh = 0.0
                if line.startswith(("$GPRMC", "$GNRMC")):
                    valid = getattr(msg, "status", "V") == "A"
                    spd = getattr(msg, "spd_over_grnd", None)
                    if spd is not None and spd != "":
                        try:
                            speed_kmh = float(spd) * _KNOTS_TO_KMH
                        except (ValueError, TypeError):
                            pass
                elif line.startswith(("$GPGGA", "$GNGGA")):
                    valid = int(getattr(msg, "gps_qual", 0) or 0) > 0

                # Empty lat/lon fields parse as 0.0 — reject as invalid
                if lat_f == 0.0 and lon_f == 0.0:
                    valid = False

                now = time.time()

                # RMC sentences carry speed; GGA sentences don't.
                # Carry forward the last RMC speed for GGA sentences
                # only if it's still fresh (< max_age).
                is_rmc = line.startswith(("$GPRMC", "$GNRMC"))
                if is_rmc:
                    self._last_speed_kmh = speed_kmh
                    self._last_speed_ts = now
                elif now - self._last_speed_ts <= self._max_age_sec:
                    speed_kmh = self._last_speed_kmh

                fix = GpsFix(
                    lat=lat_f, lon=lon_f, ts=now,
                    valid=bool(valid), speed_kmh=speed_kmh,
                )
                with self._lock:
                    self._latest = fix
                    if fix.valid:
                        self._last_valid = fix

            except Exception:
                continue


def create_gps_reader(logger: Any) -> Optional[GPSReader]:
    """Create a GPSReader from env vars, or return None if disabled/unavailable."""

    if not _parse_bool(os.getenv("GPS_ENABLED"), default=False):
        return None

    try:
        import serial  # type: ignore
        import pynmea2  # type: ignore
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning("GPS disabled (missing dependency): %s", exc)
        return None

    port = os.getenv("GPS_PORT", "/dev/ttyACM0")
    baud = _parse_int(os.getenv("GPS_BAUD"), 9600)
    max_age = _parse_float(os.getenv("GPS_FIX_MAX_AGE_SEC"), 2.0)

    try:
        return GPSReader(
            port=port,
            baud=baud,
            max_age_sec=max_age,
            logger=logger,
            serial_module=serial,
            nmea_module=pynmea2,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning("GPS init failed port=%s baud=%s error=%s", port, baud, exc)
        return None

"""Logging setup."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime


def setup_logging(log_dir: str, logger_name: str = "edge_inference") -> logging.Logger:
    """Configure logging handlers and return the named logger."""
    os.makedirs(log_dir, exist_ok=True)
    log_path = os.path.join(
        log_dir, f"edge_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}.log"
    )

    logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    logger.propagate = False  # keep output predictable even if root logger is configured elsewhere

    # Replace existing handlers to avoid duplicates across restarts.
    for handler in list(logger.handlers):
        logger.removeHandler(handler)

    formatter = logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s")

    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path)
    file_handler.setFormatter(formatter)

    stream_handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
    stream_handler.setFormatter(formatter)

    logger.addHandler(file_handler)
    logger.addHandler(stream_handler)
    logger.info("Logging to %s", log_path)
    return logger

"""Combined UI: live video preview and control buttons."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from typing import Callable, Optional

import cv2


def is_shutdown_ui_supported(logger=None) -> bool:
    if not os.getenv("DISPLAY"):
        if logger:
            logger.warning("Shutdown UI disabled: DISPLAY is not set")
        return False
    try:
        import gi

        gi.require_version("Gtk", "3.0")
        from gi.repository import Gtk  # noqa: F401
    except Exception as exc:
        if logger:
            logger.warning("Shutdown UI disabled: Gtk unavailable (%s)", exc)
        return False
    return True


class ShutdownUI:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        enabled: bool,
        logger,
        on_shutdown_request: Callable[[], None],
        show_stop_button: bool = True,
        show_poweroff_button: bool = True,
        frame_provider: Optional[Callable[[], object]] = None,
        frame_is_rgb: bool = False,
    ):
        self._enabled_requested = enabled
        self._logger = logger
        self._on_shutdown_request = on_shutdown_request
        self._show_stop_button = bool(show_stop_button)
        self._show_poweroff_button = bool(show_poweroff_button)
        self._frame_provider = frame_provider
        self._frame_is_rgb = bool(frame_is_rgb)
        self._stop_requested = False
        self._shutdown_requested = False
        self._window = None
        self._video_frame = None
        self._video_area = None
        self._menu_frame = None
        self._stop_btn = None
        self._shutdown_btn = None
        self._css_provider = None
        self._refresh_source_id = 0
        self._latest_rgb_bytes = b""
        self._latest_pixbuf = None
        self._scaled_pixbuf = None
        self._scaled_key = None  # (pixbuf_id, area_w, area_h)
        self._screen_w = 1280
        self._screen_h = 720
        self.enabled = False

    def start(self) -> None:
        if not self._enabled_requested:
            return
        if not is_shutdown_ui_supported(self._logger):
            return

        import gi

        gi.require_version("Gtk", "3.0")
        from gi.repository import Gdk, GLib, Gtk

        self._gdk = Gdk
        self._glib = GLib
        self._gtk = Gtk

        window = Gtk.Window(title="Road Monitoring")
        screen = Gdk.Screen.get_default()
        if screen is not None:
            screen_w = max(640, int(screen.get_width()))
            screen_h = max(480, int(screen.get_height()))
            self._screen_w = screen_w
            self._screen_h = screen_h
            window.set_default_size(screen_w, screen_h)
            window.resize(screen_w, screen_h)
        else:
            window.set_default_size(1280, 720)
            self._screen_w = 1280
            self._screen_h = 720
        window.fullscreen()
        window.connect("delete-event", self._on_window_close)
        window.connect("size-allocate", self._on_size_allocate)

        root_box = Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.HORIZONTAL, spacing=8)
        root_box.set_border_width(8)

        video_frame = Gtk.Frame()
        video_frame.set_shadow_type(Gtk.ShadowType.IN)
        video_frame.set_hexpand(True)
        video_frame.set_vexpand(True)
        video_frame.get_style_context().add_class("video-frame")

        video_area = Gtk.DrawingArea()
        video_area.set_hexpand(True)
        video_area.set_vexpand(True)
        video_area.set_halign(Gtk.Align.FILL)
        video_area.set_valign(Gtk.Align.FILL)
        video_area.set_size_request(1, 1)
        video_area.connect("draw", self._on_video_draw)
        video_frame.add(video_area)

        menu_frame = Gtk.Frame()
        menu_frame.set_shadow_type(Gtk.ShadowType.IN)
        menu_frame.set_hexpand(False)
        menu_frame.set_vexpand(True)
        menu_frame.get_style_context().add_class("menu-frame")

        menu_box = Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL, spacing=0)
        menu_box.set_border_width(12)
        menu_box.set_halign(Gtk.Align.FILL)
        menu_box.set_valign(Gtk.Align.FILL)

        controls_box = Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL, spacing=12)
        controls_box.set_halign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        controls_box.set_valign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)

        stop_box = Gtk.Frame()
        stop_box.set_shadow_type(Gtk.ShadowType.IN)
        stop_box.set_halign(Gtk.Align.FILL)
        stop_box.get_style_context().add_class("stop-box")

        stop_box_inner = Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL, spacing=0)
        stop_box_inner.set_border_width(10)
        stop_box_inner.set_halign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        stop_box_inner.set_valign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)

        stop_btn = Gtk.Button(label="Stop")
        stop_btn.connect("clicked", self._on_stop_click)
        stop_btn.set_halign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        stop_btn.set_valign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        stop_btn.get_style_context().add_class("stop-btn")

        stop_box_inner.pack_start(stop_btn, False, False, 0)
        stop_box.add(stop_box_inner)
        if self._show_stop_button:
            controls_box.pack_start(stop_box, False, False, 0)

        shutdown_box = Gtk.Frame()
        shutdown_box.set_shadow_type(Gtk.ShadowType.IN)
        shutdown_box.set_halign(Gtk.Align.FILL)
        shutdown_box.get_style_context().add_class("shutdown-box")

        shutdown_box_inner = Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL, spacing=0)
        shutdown_box_inner.set_border_width(10)
        shutdown_box_inner.set_halign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        shutdown_box_inner.set_valign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)

        shutdown_btn = Gtk.Button(label="Shutdown")
        shutdown_btn.connect("clicked", self._on_shutdown_click)
        shutdown_btn.set_halign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        shutdown_btn.set_valign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        shutdown_btn.get_style_context().add_class("shutdown-btn")

        shutdown_box_inner.pack_start(shutdown_btn, False, False, 0)
        shutdown_box.add(shutdown_box_inner)
        if self._show_poweroff_button:
            controls_box.pack_start(shutdown_box, False, False, 0)

        button_center = Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL, spacing=0)
        button_center.set_hexpand(True)
        button_center.set_vexpand(True)
        button_center.set_halign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        button_center.set_valign(Gtk.Align.CENTER)
        button_center.pack_start(controls_box, False, False, 0)

        menu_box.pack_start(button_center, True, True, 0)
        menu_frame.add(menu_box)

        root_box.pack_start(video_frame, True, True, 0)
        root_box.pack_start(menu_frame, False, True, 0)
        window.add(root_box)

        self._apply_layout_css(button_font_px=30)

        window.show_all()

        self._window = window
        self._video_frame = video_frame
        self._video_area = video_area
        self._menu_frame = menu_frame
        self._stop_btn = stop_btn
        self._shutdown_btn = shutdown_btn
        self.enabled = True
        self._logger.info("Shutdown UI enabled (single-window mode)")
        self._on_size_allocate(window, window.get_allocation())

        if self._frame_provider is not None:
            self._refresh_source_id = GLib.timeout_add(33, self._refresh_video_frame)

    def stop(self) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        if self._refresh_source_id:
            try:
                self._glib.source_remove(self._refresh_source_id)
            except Exception:
                pass
            self._refresh_source_id = 0
        if self._window is not None:
            try:
                self._window.destroy()
            except Exception as exc:
                self._logger.warning("Failed to close shutdown UI cleanly: %s", exc)
        self._window = None
        self._video_frame = None
        self._video_area = None
        self._menu_frame = None
        self._stop_btn = None
        self._shutdown_btn = None
        self._css_provider = None
        self._latest_pixbuf = None
        self._scaled_pixbuf = None
        self._scaled_key = None
        self.enabled = False

    def was_requested(self) -> bool:
        return self._shutdown_requested

    def was_shutdown_requested(self) -> bool:
        return self._shutdown_requested

    def was_stop_requested(self) -> bool:
        return self._stop_requested

    def _refresh_video_frame(self) -> bool:
        if self._frame_provider is None or self._video_area is None:
            return True
        frame = self._frame_provider()
        if frame is None:
            return True
        if not hasattr(frame, "shape") or len(frame.shape) != 3:
            return True

        if self._frame_is_rgb:
            rgb = frame
        else:
            try:
                rgb = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
            except Exception:
                return True

        frame_h, frame_w = rgb.shape[:2]
        if frame_h <= 0 or frame_w <= 0:
            return True

        from gi.repository import GdkPixbuf

        self._latest_rgb_bytes = rgb.tobytes()
        bytes_obj = self._glib.Bytes.new(self._latest_rgb_bytes)
        self._latest_pixbuf = GdkPixbuf.Pixbuf.new_from_bytes(
            bytes_obj,
            GdkPixbuf.Colorspace.RGB,
            False,
            8,
            frame_w,
            frame_h,
            frame_w * 3,
        )
        self._video_area.queue_draw()
        return True

    def _on_video_draw(self, widget, cr):
        pixbuf = self._latest_pixbuf
        if pixbuf is None:
            return False

        from gi.repository import Gdk, GdkPixbuf

        area_w = max(1, int(widget.get_allocated_width()))
        area_h = max(1, int(widget.get_allocated_height()))
        src_w = max(1, int(pixbuf.get_width()))
        src_h = max(1, int(pixbuf.get_height()))

        scale = min(area_w / src_w, area_h / src_h)
        draw_w = max(1, int(src_w * scale))
        draw_h = max(1, int(src_h * scale))
        x = max(0, int((area_w - draw_w) / 2))
        y = max(0, int((area_h - draw_h) / 2))

        cache_key = (id(pixbuf), area_w, area_h)
        if cache_key == self._scaled_key and self._scaled_pixbuf is not None:
            scaled = self._scaled_pixbuf
        elif draw_w != src_w or draw_h != src_h:
            scaled = pixbuf.scale_simple(draw_w, draw_h, GdkPixbuf.InterpType.BILINEAR)
            self._scaled_pixbuf = scaled
            self._scaled_key = cache_key
        else:
            scaled = pixbuf
            self._scaled_pixbuf = scaled
            self._scaled_key = cache_key

        Gdk.cairo_set_source_pixbuf(cr, scaled, x, y)
        cr.paint()
        return False

    def _on_stop_click(self, _button) -> None:
        if self._stop_requested or self._shutdown_requested:
            return
        self._stop_requested = True
        self._deactivate_controls()
        self._logger.warning("Stop button pressed; stopping application")
        try:
            self._on_shutdown_request()
        except Exception as exc:
            self._logger.error("Failed to request app stop from UI: %s", exc)

    def _on_shutdown_click(self, _button) -> None:
        if self._stop_requested or self._shutdown_requested:
            return
        self._shutdown_requested = True
        self._deactivate_controls()
        self._logger.warning("Shutdown button pressed; stopping application")
        try:
            self._on_shutdown_request()
        except Exception as exc:
            self._logger.error("Failed to request app shutdown from UI: %s", exc)

    def _deactivate_controls(self) -> None:
        for button in (self._stop_btn, self._shutdown_btn):
            if button is None:
                continue
            try:
                button.set_sensitive(False)
            except Exception:
                pass
        if self._window is not None:
            try:
                self._window.hide()
            except Exception:
                pass

    def _on_window_close(self, *_args):
        # Keep the window available so shutdown control is always present.
        return True

    def _on_size_allocate(self, _widget, allocation) -> None:
        if self._menu_frame is None or self._stop_btn is None:
            return

        total_w = max(1, int(allocation.width))
        total_h = max(1, int(allocation.height))
        if total_w < 40 or total_h < 40:
            return
        if self._window is not None and (
            total_w > self._screen_w + 2 or total_h > self._screen_h + 2
        ):
            self._window.resize(self._screen_w, self._screen_h)
            return

        menu_w = int(total_w * 0.22)
        menu_w = max(120, min(menu_w, 420))
        menu_w = min(menu_w, max(80, total_w - 80))
        self._menu_frame.set_size_request(menu_w, -1)

        base_scale = min(total_w / 1280.0, total_h / 720.0)
        base_scale = max(0.65, min(base_scale, 1.8))

        btn_w = int(menu_w * 0.78)
        btn_w = max(84, min(btn_w, max(84, menu_w - 16)))
        btn_h = int(95 * base_scale)
        btn_h = max(42, min(btn_h, 180))
        if self._stop_btn is not None and self._show_stop_button:
            self._stop_btn.set_size_request(btn_w, btn_h)
        if self._shutdown_btn is not None and self._show_poweroff_button:
            self._shutdown_btn.set_size_request(btn_w, btn_h)

        button_font_px = int(28 * base_scale)
        self._apply_layout_css(
            button_font_px=max(18, button_font_px),
        )

    def _apply_layout_css(self, *, button_font_px: int) -> None:
        css = f"""
frame.video-frame {{
    border: 3px solid #ff7a1a;
}}
frame.menu-frame {{
    border: 3px solid #ffbf66;
    background: #f7f7f7;
}}
frame.shutdown-box {{
    border: 3px solid #ff7a1a;
    background: #ffffff;
}}
frame.stop-box {{
    border: 3px solid #1e88e5;
    background: #ffffff;
}}
button.shutdown-btn {{
    border: 4px solid #ffffff;
    border-radius: 12px;
    background: #b00020;
    color: #ffffff;
    font-size: {button_font_px}px;
    font-weight: 800;
    padding: 10px 20px;
}}
button.shutdown-btn:hover {{
    background: #c1122f;
}}
button.stop-btn {{
    border: 4px solid #ffffff;
    border-radius: 12px;
    background: #1565c0;
    color: #ffffff;
    font-size: {button_font_px}px;
    font-weight: 800;
    padding: 10px 20px;
}}
button.stop-btn:hover {{
    background: #1976d2;
}}
"""
        if self._css_provider is None:
            self._css_provider = self._gtk.CssProvider()
            self._gtk.StyleContext.add_provider_for_screen(
                self._gdk.Screen.get_default(),
                self._css_provider,
                self._gtk.STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_APPLICATION,
            )
        self._css_provider.load_from_data(css.encode("utf-8"))


def create_shutdown_ui(
    *,
    enabled: bool,
    logger,
    on_shutdown_request: Callable[[], None],
    show_stop_button: bool = True,
    show_poweroff_button: bool = True,
    frame_provider: Optional[Callable[[], object]] = None,
    frame_is_rgb: bool = False,
) -> ShutdownUI:
    ui = ShutdownUI(
        enabled=enabled,
        logger=logger,
        on_shutdown_request=on_shutdown_request,
        show_stop_button=show_stop_button,
        show_poweroff_button=show_poweroff_button,
        frame_provider=frame_provider,
        frame_is_rgb=frame_is_rgb,
    )
    ui.start()
    return ui

"""Environment validation helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging


def validate_environment(
    api_url: str,
    api_key: str,
    aws_access_key: str,
    aws_secret_key: str,
    logger: logging.Logger,
) -> None:
    """Validate required environment variables and exit on failure."""
    missing = []
    if not api_url:
        missing.append("ROBOLYZE_API_URL")
    if not api_key:
        missing.append("ROBOLYZE_API_KEY")
    if not aws_access_key:
        missing.append("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID")
    if not aws_secret_key:
        missing.append("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY")

    if missing:
        logger.error("Missing required environment variables: %s", ", ".join(missing))
        raise SystemExit(1)

=== /home/rasp/miniproj_epan/hailo-rpi5-examples/utils/wait_for_speed.py ===
"""Wait for vehicle to reach minimum GPS speed before exiting.

Standalone script called from run_detection_fps.sh to gate pipeline startup
until the vehicle is actually moving.

Env vars:
    GPS_ENABLED, GPS_PORT, GPS_BAUD, GPS_FIX_MAX_AGE_SEC — passed through to GPSReader
    MIN_SPEED_KMH  — minimum speed to consider "moving" (default: 3.0)
    GPS_SPEED_GATE_TIMEOUT_SEC — max wait for GPS hardware/fix before giving up (default: 120)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import sys
import time

# Ensure project root is on sys.path so `utils.gps` can be imported
# when this script is invoked directly from the repo root.
_PROJECT_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
if _PROJECT_ROOT not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _PROJECT_ROOT)

from utils.gps import create_gps_reader, _parse_float  # noqa: E402

POLL_INTERVAL_SEC = 2.0


def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO,
        format="[%(asctime)s] %(message)s",
        datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    )
    logger = logging.getLogger("wait_for_speed")

    min_speed = _parse_float(os.getenv("MIN_SPEED_KMH"), 3.0)

    # Force GPS_ENABLED so we can create a reader even if .env isn't loaded yet
    os.environ.setdefault("GPS_ENABLED", "1")

    gps_timeout = _parse_float(os.getenv("GPS_SPEED_GATE_TIMEOUT_SEC"), 120.0)
    deadline = time.time() + gps_timeout

    # Retry GPS reader creation until success or timeout
    reader = None
    while reader is None:
        reader = create_gps_reader(logger)
        if reader is not None:
            break
        if time.time() >= deadline:
            logger.warning(
                "GPS unavailable after %.0fs — skipping speed gate.", gps_timeout,
            )
            return 0
        logger.info("  GPS not ready, retrying in %.0fs...", POLL_INTERVAL_SEC)
        time.sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_SEC)

    try:
        # Phase A: wait for a valid GPS fix (timeout applies here)
        logger.info("Waiting for valid GPS fix (timeout: %.0fs) ...", gps_timeout)
        got_fix = False
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if reader.get_speed() is not None:
                got_fix = True
                break
            logger.info("  No valid GPS fix yet — %.0fs remaining",
                         deadline - time.time())
            time.sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_SEC)

        if not got_fix:
            logger.warning(
                "No GPS fix after %.0fs — skipping speed gate.", gps_timeout,
            )
            return 0

        # Phase B: GPS works — wait indefinitely for vehicle to move
        # Poll every 2s for responsiveness, but only log every 10s while stationary.
        LOG_INTERVAL_SEC = 10.0
        logger.info("GPS fix acquired. Waiting for speed >= %.1f km/h ...", min_speed)
        last_log = 0.0
        while True:
            speed = reader.get_speed()
            if speed is not None and speed >= min_speed:
                logger.info("Vehicle moving at %.1f km/h — proceeding.", speed)
                return 0
            now = time.time()
            if now - last_log >= LOG_INTERVAL_SEC:
                if speed is not None:
                    logger.info("  Speed: %.1f km/h (below %.1f threshold)",
                                speed, min_speed)
                else:
                    logger.info("  Waiting for GPS fix...")
                last_log = now
            time.sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_SEC)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        logger.info("Interrupted.")
        return 130
    finally:
        reader.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

=== /home/rasp/miniproj_epan/hailo-rpi5-examples/utils/find_camera.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Locate the road camera on the LAN, even when its IP has drifted onto a
# different subnet than ours.
#
# Why this exists: on 2026-07-24 the truck LAN moved to 192.168.1.0/24 but the
# camera kept a static 192.168.0.126 in its own flash. run_detection_fps.sh then
# retried a dead address for three hours with no indication of the cause.
#
# ONVIF WS-Discovery does NOT solve this: the camera receives the multicast
# probe, but its unicast reply is routed to a gateway that does not exist on our
# subnet, so it never arrives. What *does* reach us regardless of addressing is
# layer-2 broadcast traffic — the camera's ARP requests for its own gateway, and
# its vendor discovery beacons. This script listens for exactly that.
#
# Strictly read-only: it probes and listens, and changes nothing.
# Always exits 0 so a caller running under `set -e` is never aborted.

set -uo pipefail

IFACE="${CAMERA_IFACE:-eth0}"
SNIFF_SECONDS="${CAMERA_SNIFF_SECONDS:-15}"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Expected camera MAC, so we can positively identify it wherever it turns up.
# Falls back to the value recorded in .env.
env_get() {
    sed -n -E "s/^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p" "$APP_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -1 | tr -d '"'\''\r' | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//'
}
CAMERA_MAC="${CAMERA_MAC:-$(env_get CAMERA_MAC)}"
CAMERA_MAC="$(tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' <<<"$CAMERA_MAC")"

say() { echo "$*"; }

OUR_CIDR="$(ip -4 -o addr show dev "$IFACE" scope global 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $4}' | head -1)"
say "interface=$IFACE address=${OUR_CIDR:-none} expected-mac=${CAMERA_MAC:-unset}"

# sudo is needed for the ARP scan and the sniffer. Degrade gracefully without it.
HAVE_SUDO=0
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null && HAVE_SUDO=1
(( HAVE_SUDO )) || say "NOTE: no passwordless sudo; skipping ARP scan and passive sniff."

# --- 1. Is it on our own subnet, just not answering on port 554? ------------
if (( HAVE_SUDO )) && command -v nmap >/dev/null && [[ -n "$OUR_CIDR" ]]; then
    SUBNET="$(ip -4 -o route show dev "$IFACE" scope link 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | head -1)"
    if [[ -n "$SUBNET" ]]; then
        say "scanning $SUBNET at ARP level ..."
        SCAN="$(sudo -n nmap -sn -PR -n "$SUBNET" 2>/dev/null)"
        HIT="$(awk '/Nmap scan report/{ip=$NF} /MAC Address/{print ip, tolower($3)}' <<<"$SCAN")"
        if [[ -n "$CAMERA_MAC" ]] && grep -qi "$CAMERA_MAC" <<<"$HIT"; then
            FOUND_IP="$(grep -i "$CAMERA_MAC" <<<"$HIT" | awk '{print $1}')"
            say "FOUND: camera MAC $CAMERA_MAC is on our subnet at $FOUND_IP"
            say "       -> update RTSP_URL/CAMERA_SOURCE in .env to rtsp://$FOUND_IP/live/mainstream"
            exit 0
        fi
        say "camera MAC not present on our subnet. Neighbours seen:"
        sed 's/^/  /' <<<"${HIT:-  (none)}"
    fi
fi

# --- 2. Listen for layer-2 chatter from anything off our subnet -------------
if (( HAVE_SUDO )) && command -v tcpdump >/dev/null; then
    say "listening ${SNIFF_SECONDS}s for off-subnet broadcast traffic ..."
    CAP="$(sudo -n timeout "$SNIFF_SECONDS" tcpdump -i "$IFACE" -n -e -l \
            'arp or (udp and ip broadcast)' 2>/dev/null)"

    # Pull "<source-ip> <source-mac>" pairs out of the capture. Note tcpdump -e
    # prints no literal "IP" token: field 2 is the source MAC, and the source
    # address sits in the token immediately before the ">" separator, as
    # "<ip>.<port>". ARP requests instead carry the sender as "tell <ip>".
    PAIRS="$(awk '
        { mac = $2 }
        /ARP, Request/ {
            for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++)
                if ($i == "tell") { ip = $(i+1); sub(/,$/, "", ip); print ip, mac }
            next
        }
        /ethertype IPv4/ {
            for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) {
                if ($i == ">" && $(i-1) ~ /^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/) {
                    n = split($(i-1), a, ".")
                    print a[1] "." a[2] "." a[3] "." a[4], mac
                    next
                }
            }
        }
    ' <<<"$CAP" | sort -u)"

    OUR_PREFIX="$(cut -d. -f1-3 <<<"${OUR_CIDR%%/*}")"
    OFFNET="$(awk -v p="^${OUR_PREFIX}\\\\." '$1 !~ p && $1 != "0.0.0.0"' <<<"$PAIRS")"

    if [[ -n "$OFFNET" ]]; then
        say "FOUND: device(s) broadcasting from OUTSIDE our subnet — almost certainly"
        say "       a static IP that did not follow a LAN change:"
        while read -r ip mac; do
            [[ -z "$ip" ]] && continue
            if [[ -n "$CAMERA_MAC" && "$mac" == "$CAMERA_MAC" ]]; then
                say "  $ip  (MAC $mac)  <-- THIS IS THE CAMERA"
            else
                say "  $ip  (MAC ${mac:-unknown})"
            fi
        done <<<"$OFFNET"
        say "       -> the camera holds a static address on the wrong subnet."
        say "          Re-address it, or temporarily: sudo ip addr add <free-ip-on-that-subnet>/24 dev $IFACE"
        exit 0
    fi
    say "no off-subnet broadcast traffic seen."
fi

say "camera NOT located. Check power, cabling, and switch link."
exit 0

### [run-detection-fps-sh]
